query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing the Pd/Pt component in FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys with an equiatomic amount of iridium (Ir) will induce a phase with lower lattice symmetry and stronger spin‐orbit coupling, thereby increasing the magnetocrystalline anisotropy and coercivity relative to the soft ferromagnetic FeCoNiPd/FeCoNiPt derivatives.
generation.material_initial_state: An almost equiatomic, single-phase FCC FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy (e.g., FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt) that exhibits high saturation magnetization but low coercivity due to its high lattice symmetry.
generation.intervention: Substitute the Pd or Pt component with an equiatomic addition of Ir to form an FeCoNiIr alloy.
generation.conditions: The alloy must remain almost equiatomic with a configurational entropy of at least 1.0R and be processed (e.g., via sputtering and rapid thermal annealing) under conditions that allow retention of the high-entropy phase and permit formation of low-symmetry chemical ordering.
generation.structural_mediator: The equiatomic incorporation of Ir promotes the formation of a low-symmetry, chemically ordered phase (potentially L10-like) and introduces pronounced spin–orbit coupling at the heavy element sites.
generation.mechanism: Ir, being a heavier transition metal, provides enhanced spin–orbit coupling relative to Pd or Pt, which helps lower the effective symmetry of the crystal lattice. This reduced symmetry enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy and facilitates stronger domain wall pinning, leading to a higher observed coercivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: The FeCoNiIr high-entropy alloy is expected to exhibit a noticeable increase in coercivity compared to the FeCoNiPd/FeCoNiPt baseline, while maintaining high saturation magnetization; the precise enhancement magnitude is uncertain but should be significant enough to transition from soft ferromagnetism to a magnet with appreciably higher coercivity.
generation.baseline: FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt high-entropy alloys known from earlier studies to display soft ferromagnetism (low coercive field) despite high saturation magnetization.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is expected to hold for equiatomic FeCoNi-based alloys processed under conditions that preserve high entropy and facilitate phase transformation (e.g., RTA-induced ordering) without excessive grain growth or phase segregation. Deviations from equiatomicity, significant second-phase precipitations, or processing outside the optimized temperature/time window may preclude the desired increase in coercivity.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative increase in coercivity and the extent of low-symmetry ordering induced by Ir remain uncertain. Competing effects of lattice distortion and possible changes in microstructure could moderate the predicted enhancement, warranting careful experimental control.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a set of films using identical processing conditions (e.g., sputtering followed by rapid thermal annealing) to prepare two series: one series of equiatomic FeCoNiPt (baseline) and another of equiatomic FeCoNiIr. Use XRD and STEM to verify the phase structure and ordering. Measure magnetic hysteresis loops (both in-plane and out-of-plane) to extract coercivity values.
measurements: Phase identification (XRD, STEM) to confirm low-symmetry ordering
Magnetic hysteresis measurements to determine coercivity (Hc), saturation magnetization (Ms), and magnetic anisotropy
Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) or similar to ensure comparable configurational entropy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the FeCoNiIr alloy does not show a statistically significant (e.g., >20%) increase in coercivity relative to the FeCoNiPt baseline (under otherwise identical conditions) or if no change in phase symmetry is observed, then the hypothesis that Ir substitution enhances coercivity via increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy would be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Certain HEA compositions may exhibit long‐range chemical order through the emergence of multiple sublattices, analogous to high entropy ceramics,[  ] leading to so‐called “high entropy intermetallic” (HEI) compounds.[  ] Previously, transition metal alloys with high anisotropy, such as the L10 phases of FePt and FePd have been achieved by annealing of equiatomic solid solution pre‐cursors.[  ] In the case of metastable high anisotropy phases such as L10 FeNi, unconventional annealing techniques have been employed.[  ] In particular, rapid thermal annealing (RTA) of transition metal alloy films on Si/SiO2 is an effective means of inducing high anisotropy phase formation in solid solution precursors, in part due to the substrate‐induced strain.[  ] In this study, we experimentally demonstrate two thin film HEAs with large coercivity and magnetic anisotropy achieved by RTA. We show that RTA treatment of equiatomic FeCoNiMnCu thin films leads to ≈40‐fold increase in coercivity. By introduction of 50 at.% Pt, we realize an L10 HEI phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy resulting from a reduced lattice symmetry and strong spin‐orbit coupling. While the combination of saturation magnetization and coercivity for these RTA‐ treated FeCoNiMnCu films is impressive in comparison to previously reported bulk systems, the coercivity is still modest, due to the high symmetry of the cubic lattice which limits the intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy. The facilitation of low‐symmetry chemical order and crystal structure combined with strong spin‐orbit coupling is in general necessary to realize strong magnetocrysalline anisotropy. To achieve these conditions in a high entropy system, we have added 50 at.% Pt to the FeCoNiMnCu alloy, employing the high entropy intermetallic design approach in search of highly anisotropic L10 ordering. Although the certainty of Pt sites reduces the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, we demonstrate below that such optimized entropy can still stabilize a single high‐entropy L10 phase.
